title: Greek theomachy as Council–Serpentine conflict memory
statement: The divine-conflict architecture of the Greek mythological tradition — the succession of heaven, the Titanomachy and the Typhoeus combat, the deliberating divine assembly, divine–human interbreeding, and the punished transfer of civilisational knowledge — preserves, in mythologically transformed shape, cultural memory of the Council–Serpentine conflict among the Elohim, anchored in the canon's naming of Greece as a creator-base region whose mythology contains testimonies.

includes: A collective, structural-level reading of five Greek structure-families as transformed conflict memory: heavenly succession, the Titanomachy and Typhoeus combat, the divine assembly, divine–human interbreeding, and the punished knowledge transfer (Prometheus)
The institutional texture of the Homeric pantheon (councils, portfolios, factions, favourites, presidency and dissent) read as memory of a governing class
A structural correspondence between Prometheus and the canon's disclosing insider: position in the plot, not identity of name or person
The proposition operates at the level of what the stories remember, not how they travelled
excludes: Any claim about transmission routes; where philology traces a route (Kumarbi to Hesiod), the route explains the resemblance and is not contested
One-to-one identification of individual Greek deities with individual Elohim
Historicity of the events of the Odyssey or of a Homeric Trojan War
Any reading of the Homeric text as eyewitness testimony; the oral-formulaic recomposition results are accepted in full
Allegorical decoding of individual monsters (Cyclops-as-volcano style readings)

alternatives.statement: The Greek–Near Eastern parallels are explained by documented literary transmission along Anatolian, Cypriot, and Levantine routes, with no remembered historical referent required.
Shared structures reflect common Indo-European poetic and mythological inheritance rather than memory of any event.

Myths converge because human minds share a common architecture; sky councils, succession conflicts, and knowledge-theft plots are what hierarchical societies' imaginations produce without any memory at all.
The pantheon's governing-class texture projects Bronze and Iron Age palace politics onto the sky; no external governing class is needed.
Oral-formulaic transmission cannot carry structural memory over the required span; the demonstrated high-fidelity horizon is roughly four centuries, far short of the corpus chronology.
The technological reading re-describes mythology in the prestige idiom of a modern age while preserving its religious structure — a modernisation, not an explanation.

revision_triggers: The motif inventory proves fully predictable from social structure and cognitive bias, vindicating the structural and projection alternatives.
